## Root Cause: `subPath` mount blocks ConfigMap hot-reload

### What we found

Both gateway pods (`api-gateway-7c9f8d6b54-x2kqp` and `api-gateway-7c9f8d6b54-r7tmw`) mount the `gateway-limits` ConfigMap using a `subPath` entry:

```
mountPath: /etc/gateway/limits.yaml
subPath:   limits.yaml
```

Kubernetes does **not** propagate ConfigMap updates to containers that use a `subPath` volume mount [cite: concepts/configuration/configmap#using-configmaps-as-files-from-a-pod-4] [cite: tasks/configure-pod-container/configure-pod-configmap#mounted-configmaps-are-updated-automatically-0]. Because of this, the file inside the container is frozen at the version that was present when the pod started (06:02 today), and the gateway's own 30-second file watcher never sees a change.

### Evidence

Both pod logs confirm this unambiguously. Every 30 s since startup the watcher reports the same hash — even after the ConfigMap was updated at 09:10:

```
2026-05-21T06:02:07Z INFO tenant=acme-logistics limit_rps=100 burst=150        ← old limit loaded at start
2026-05-21T09:12:30Z INFO limits watcher: /etc/gateway/limits.yaml unchanged (sha256=9c1e4b07)
2026-05-21T11:29:30Z INFO limits watcher: /etc/gateway/limits.yaml unchanged (sha256=9c1e4b07)  ← still the same hash
```

Meanwhile, the 429s continue at the old 100 rps limit:

```
2026-05-21T11:29:05Z WARN 429 tenant=acme-logistics limit_rps=100 observed_rps=204 rejected=2087
```

### Immediate fix (gets acme-logistics unblocked today)

Roll out a restart of the gateway Deployment so the new pods start with the updated ConfigMap value already baked into the mounted file:

```bash
kubectl rollout restart deployment/api-gateway -n edge
kubectl rollout status  deployment/api-gateway -n edge
```

This is safe — the Deployment will do a rolling restart, keeping existing pods alive until the new ones are ready.

### Permanent fix (prevents recurrence)

Remove the `subPath` from the volume mount in the Deployment spec and mount the full directory instead. Kubernetes' kubelet will then automatically propagate ConfigMap updates to the mounted files (with up to ~2 minutes of propagation delay [cite: tasks/configure-pod-container/configure-pod-configmap#mounted-configmaps-are-updated-automatically-0]), and the gateway's file watcher will detect the change without any pod restart.

```yaml
# Change this:
volumeMounts:
  - name: limits
    mountPath: /etc/gateway/limits.yaml
    subPath: limits.yaml

# To this:
volumeMounts:
  - name: limits
    mountPath: /etc/gateway/limits   # mount the whole directory
# Then reference /etc/gateway/limits/limits.yaml in gateway config
```

### Side note (separate ticket recommended)

Both pods are logging repeated Redis i/o timeouts when syncing rate counters (`redis-limits.edge.svc:6379`). While not the cause of this ticket, it means each pod is enforcing the 100 rps limit independently using local counters rather than a shared counter — so the combined rejected traffic is higher than it would otherwise be. This warrants a separate investigation.
